name: VA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with PVI of D+18
Long-serving incumbent Bobby Scott running for re-election
Republican challenger raised only about $6,600 with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at roughly 95%
model.rationale: Bobby Scott holds a D+18 district with incumbency advantages and a large fundraising edge, while Edwin Rivera's campaign is essentially unfunded. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: A major outside spending push for Rivera or an unexpected incumbent scandal would be the only plausible route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bobby Scott, a long-serving Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a southeastern Virginia district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan baseline of D+18. He has raised nearly $700,000 for the campaign, while Republican nominee Edwin Rivera has raised under $7,000 and reports minimal cash on hand. Two independent candidates are also on the ballot but lack significant resources.

No public general-election polling exists for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 95 percent. The combination of district partisanship, incumbency, and the funding gap makes this seat a safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the winning margin rather than the outcome.
